answer: Atlas Coordination Price. Each new identity must publish a distinct, verifiable data asset (a "pearl") before its actions count toward any quorum. A random-sample audit panel scores asset novelty against the existing corpus; duplicated or templated submissions fail, and the identity's votes are voided. Rejected identities must resubmit with a fresh ridge of provenance metadata, paying full audit cost each round. Sybils therefore pay real compute plus repeated audit fees per identity, while genuine agents amortize one asset across many actions.
